newsitem.title: USA: Bonds help fuel holiday rally for stocks.
newsitem.headline: Bonds help fuel holiday rally for stocks.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks resumed their rally in a shortened holiday session Friday, a day after the Thanksgiving holiday, as long-term interest rates tumbled and retailers geared up for a strong holiday shopping season.
The technology-studded Nasdaq Composite index set its fifth consecutive record high.
After two sessions of losses, the Dow Jones industrial average rallied 22.36 points to close at 6,521.70, up 49.94 on the week.
In the broader market, gainers outpaced losers by 1,305 to 906 on very light volume of 149.8 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange as many traders stayed home for a long holiday weekend.
The Nasdaq index rose 5.29 to a record 1,292.61, and gained 18.25 for the week.
Trading on the NYSE, Nasdaq and the American Stock Exchange closed at 1 p.m. EST.

Stocks took their cue from the bond market, where the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose nearly one full point, knocking the yield down to 6.36 percent, the lowest close since its March 4, vs. 6.45 percent Wednesday.

"The market still has an upward bias, so unless we get some bad news, it's going to keep going up. Also, it's apparently going to be a good Christmas for retailers," said Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage.

Despite a shorter post-Thanksgiving buying season, analysts are expecting holiday sales to jump about 5 percent over last year's disappointing season due to higher consumer confidence and strong employment.

"The stock market knows no bounds," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "It's going to be a strong Christmas season for retailers, and the economy is no longer tepid. This economy is stable on the pricing side, yet running full steam ahead, and we're in a strong second half of the fourth quarter."
Among technology issues on the Nasdaq, Intel Corp. added 1/4 to 126-7/8 and Microsoft Corp. gained 1-3/8 to 156-7/8.

U.S. Robotics Corp. rose 4-1/2 to 78 in heavy trading. The maker of computer modems said its products will be included in Dell Computer Corp.'s Dimension line of personal computers early next year. Dell rose 1-5/8 to 101-5/8.
Unisys shares were the most active on the NYSE, jumping 1-1/8 to 7-5/8 after a published report that the computer mainframe maker might post a profit in 1997.
International Business Machines Corp. shares also rose, gaining 1-1/4 to 159-3/8.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 2.02 to 757.02. The index was up 8.29 for the week.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.95 to 398.43, up 3.77 on the week. The average price per share was up 10 cents.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.84 to 591.48, and added 0.71 on the week.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,292.158, up 22.641, or 0.31 percent. The index rose 81.563 from a week ago.
